role.altitude: The detective keeps judging when to call for help, working undercover and listening to what matters on authorised taps; describing locations by radio, logging calls and typing first transcripts shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Checking machine transcripts against the audio before quoting them
role.ambitious_version: A detective who hears the key call the day it is made instead of days later.

tasks.short: Assess the situation, notify command of the situation and request assistance, brief arriving colleagues and record the notification in the incident log.

steps.what: Detective assesses the situation and decides assistance is needed
Detective notifies command by radio or phone of the situation and location and requests assistance
Detective records the notification and the assistance received in the incident log

tasks.design: Judging and calling for help stay with the detective. The detective's radio or phone shares its position with the control room, so the location does not have to be described in words. The control room's incident system logs the call and the units sent, and that record is linked to the case, so the detective only adds what happened.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locations were described by voice and the call was logged twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Radios and phones that share position with the control room, and incident logs linked to cases.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when to call for help before it is needed.

evidence.claim: Police radios and phones can share their position with a control room.
Position data of officers can monitor staff and need works council consent if used that way.

assumptions: Boundary: from deciding to call for help to the log entry; the response itself is outside.
Input contract for s4: the call and dispatched units recorded by the control room's incident system and linked to the case.
Position sharing is used for the incident, not to monitor officers.
Assessing, calling and briefing keep their full or nearly full time.

s2 keeps 90 because the location no longer has to be described and the call itself stays; s4 keeps 50 because the call and units come from the control room's record and the detective writes what happened.
unknowns: How often detectives call for assistance.

incremental.description: Detective checks the linked incident record in the case.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: position sharing fails indoors and many records are not linked to the case (2.7); high: positions and links work as designed (9.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform undercover assignments and maintain surveillance in the field, monitor authorized wiretaps, summarise and transcribe relevant calls, and write surveillance reports.

steps.what: Detective performs undercover assignments and maintains surveillance in the field
Detective monitors authorized wiretaps by listening to intercepted calls

loop.input: Intercepted calls in the language of the investigation, transcribed on police servers.
loop.output: A text transcript per call with time codes, for skimming.
loop.check: Transcripts are for triage only; the detective listens to every call marked relevant and to every call whose transcript is unclear or has low confidence, and nothing is quoted from a transcript without checking the audio; foreign-language calls go to a sworn interpreter.
loop.why_not_simpler: Hours of calls cannot be skimmed as audio.

steps.what: Detective writes summaries and transcripts of relevant calls

tasks.design: Field surveillance and undercover work stay fully human. Intercepted calls in the investigation's language are transcribed on police servers so the detective can skim text and listen to the calls that matter; the corrected transcript of a relevant passage is the start of the call report. Foreign-language calls go to sworn interpreters as today. Surveillance reports are written by the detective. No biometric identification or profiling is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every intercepted call had to be listened to in full before anything could be written.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-to-text that can run on police servers.
tasks.still_hard: Coded language and slang on the line.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a suspect means rather than what they say.
tasks.altitude: Faster triage of taps; surveillance stays human.

reach.learn: Whether triage sends fewer irrelevant calls for translation.

evidence.claim: The police run their own language model on police servers.
Real-time remote biometric identification in public needs prior authorisation; profiling-based offence prediction is banned.
High-risk processing of police data needs a DPIA, and automated decisions with adverse effect need human intervention.

assumptions: Boundary: surveillance and monitoring of authorised taps; obtaining the authorisation is outside.

Input contract for s2: intercepted calls delivered to the police interception system under a magistrate's order; about 70% are in the investigation's language and are transcribed; the rest go to interpreters; s2 is priced at that share.
Field work and surveillance reports keep their full time.
unknowns: Hours of intercepted calls per case.

already_counted.description: Detective checks transcript passages against the audio before quoting them.

incremental.description: Detective reports systematic transcription errors on names and slang.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: transcripts are poor on slang and names, so most calls are still listened to in full and typed (5.5); high: about 70% of calls transcribed well enough for triage as assumed (13.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
